newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-HINGIS WINS AUSTRALIAN OPEN, MAKES HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS WINS AUSTRALIAN OPEN, MAKES HISTORY.

text.p: Swiss teenager Martina Hingis became the youngest Grand Slam champion in modern tennis history on Saturday when she stormed past former champion Mary Pierce in the final of the Australian Open.
Calmly stepping up her game whenever the Frenchwoman looked threatening, the 16-year-old beat Pierce 6-2 6-2.

At 16 years and three months, Hingis became the youngest singles champion at one of the sport's four major championships since amateur Lottie Dod won Wimbledon at 15 years and 10 months in 1887 -- before the idea of the Grand Slam was invented.
Hingis had already become the youngest Grand Slam champion ever by winning the women's doubles at Wimbledon last year.

The Czechoslovak-born world number four started the match as hot favourite after cruising through the woman's draw in Melbourne. The only doubt had been whether she might be hit by nerves in her first Grand Slam singles final.

But she saved three break points in the first game and never really looked back, taming Pierce's powerful groundstrokes with near-perfect precision tennis. The unseeded Pierce, 22, won in Melbourne in 1995 but has not claimed any major titles since then.
